utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer to that question, Mrs. Mladic. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we can go back to page 1 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page in the English -- I'm not sure that's the -- yeah. That first paragraph there, you state that: "I went with my husband, Ratko Mladic, to the wedding of Biljana Djurdjevic and Zarko Stojkovic in the church in Admirala Geprata Street on 16 July 1995. I remember the exact date because it was four days after Petrovdan day and my husband had arrived in Belgrade two days before." You go on to say: "I remember that he got up early on 14 and 15 July and went to some meetings ..." I'm going to stop there. Now, you say in your statement that you reviewed, you had no objections to, and you signed, that you remember he got up early on the 14th of July. So, according to this statement, your husband was with you on the morning of the 14th July. Presumably you're -- I understand this statement to mean he was there sometime the night of the 13th or early morning hours on the 14th. Today and in your statement that you provided in July 2014, you say that your husband arrived on the evening of 14th of July. So, Mrs. Mladic, which of these two versions would you like us to accept as the truth as you claim it to be?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: He got up in the morning of the 14th and the 15th. He was in the house. So he came in the evening of the 14th and then went to meetings in the morning -- I mean, during the night, late at night he came at home, and we woke up on the morning of the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Inaudible]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear any of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, one second, please. Since you are holding your hands before your mouth, the interpreters cannot hear you. Can you please restart your answer. And perhaps Ms. Hasan again puts the question to you so that we have everything in full on the record. Perhaps if you bend over a little bit to the right, that you should take care that the microphone is close enough to ... Ms. Hasan, could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Essentially, Mrs. Mladic, what I want to know is which version of the two statements of your account of what happened on the 14th of July do you want us to accept as the truth: The one which says that he arrived in Belgrade and you remember he got up early on the 14th and 15th of July and went to some meetings; or the version where you say he arrived in the evening hours of 14th July?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, this statement that I gave in July 2014.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So were you not telling the truth when you provided this statement to the high court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: It's not that I wasn't telling the truth. At that moment I probably couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you were mistaken about that, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was mistaken. I was mistaken, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Turning to the day of the wedding, do you recall what time you left your house that morning, the morning of the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: We got ready in the morning and -- it wasn't that early. We were there probably around 10.00. Other members of the wedding party had already arrived; that is to say, the bride and bridegroom were there, the bridegroom's parents, then Biljana Djurdjevic's mother, and her people. So we arrived at the end, Ratko and I.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just to follow-up on this answer to your question, the -- you say here that: "We were probably there around 10.00 ..." And I take it that you are referring to arriving at the bride's apartment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the time we arrived at the bride's apartment. Now, whether it was quarter to 10.00 or 10.00, but it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And as you provide in your statement, you then proceed to go to the ceremony in the church, and you leave thereafter to the restaurant Dva Ribara to return home at about 6.00 p.m. that day.

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Around that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, how long did the journey take you from the restaurant to your home?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Well, say, around half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, according to you, you arrive at your home at about 6.30 p.m.; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly. Well, you know what, I mean, I cannot say whether it's ten minutes more or less. But approximately. I mean, really, I wasn't looking at my watch and writing things down.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So your husband, he, once you arrive at home, he leaves the vehicle, and, as I understand it, he went to the apartment to change into his uniform; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No. We returned together from Biljana Djurdjevic's and Zarko's. We returned home together. But my husband changed. And since I wore that dress, the only one that wasn't completely dark, I wore that dress.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. But when you arrived in the vehicle with driver Kenjic and your husband at your home that evening, did you enter the apartment with your husband, or did you stay and wait in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the 16th of July, are we?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, after you leave the restaurant, you say that you went home at about 6.30. You claim it took you about a half an hour to get home and that your husband then changed into his uniform. I just want to know, did you enter the apartment with your husband? Did you stay waiting for him in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, no. I entered the apartment with my husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How much time when you say you spent in the apartment before you left to the VMA?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Well, not a lot of time. Just enough time for him to change.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Ten minutes, 15 minutes, an hour?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Well, say, 15, 20 minutes. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was anyone else besides you and your husband in the apartment?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, no one. Because at that time my son was on summer vacation with his girlfriend.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So then you drive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, are you on -- moving --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to another subject?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm not, but we can -- I know that it is the time for the break, and I can just pause there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Mladic, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We would like to see you back after the break. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be brought in, Ms. Hasan, and I'm also looking at you, Mr. Lukic, that statement before the Belgrade court was apparently in a criminal case?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This was pursuant to a request from the OTP to the war crimes department to investigate -- to conduct an investigation into the video that was taken at the VMA on the 16th of July, and this hearing that took place was part and parcel of the investigation they conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's also why you are recorded, if it's at least you, Mr. Lukic, to be present. Although, maybe someone else. But that you were there as counsel for Mr. -- No loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no translation at all in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh. If there is no translation, we should seek the assistance of technicians and/or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's okay now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see Mr. Mladic is nodding yes. You were present as Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was there with Mr. Sajlic who was actually Mrs. Mladic's lawyer. And I was recorded, and I was there, I think, only at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why I was recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- [Overlapping speakers] ... it was only Mr. Sajlic was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that counsel are present in a context in which they apparently then represent a witness at the same time being involved in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My -- my assumption was that Mrs. Mladic was the witness at that moment, not that there was no proceedings against her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that there were. But, of course, I was wondering. I saw that you and Mr. Sajlic were present, at least that's what's recorded. And, of course, I asked myself in what capacity you were there and in what capacity Mr. Sajlic was there. And what may -- well, I'm just seeking at this moment to establish these facts. I leave it to that. Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We left off, Mrs. Mladic, talking about the evening of the 16th of July. And now once Mr. Mladic changed into his uniform, you said you spent, I believe it was given or take, 15 minutes at the apartment and then you proceeded to the VMA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Our investigation has revealed that it takes about -- it's about 13 kilometres to the VMA from your apartment, so it would take approximately 13 or so minutes to get there. Is that about right, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember how much time it took us to get there. It depends on the traffic, too. Sometimes it's a bit longer. And then if there is no traffic, it's quicker.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, Mrs. Mladic, you do recall arriving at the VMA in the evening; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It was still light outside?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, light.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, are you familiar with Ned Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you know who Ned Krajisnik is? He was present at the VMA at this meeting that you attended?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember him. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Milan Lesic?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And he too was also present at this meeting at the VMA that you attended?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, Mrs. Mladic, both Ned Krajisnik and Milan Lesic who attended this meeting with you have testified before this Tribunal, and I'm just going to read you very short portions from their testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we take a look at 32880. That's 65 ter. And this is the testimony of Ned Krajisnik. It's in the Perisic case on the 2nd of November, 2009. And if we turn to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Line 22, he was asked: "Do you recall approximately what time of day this meeting in the VMA board room was taking place?" Answer --

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Sorry, this is in English and I don't understand English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, I should have explained this to you before I started. But I will read it out to you so you can hear it in a language you understand. So --

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- let me start again. "Q. Do you recall approximately what time of day this meeting in the VMA boardroom was taking place? "A. I believe it was late afternoon." Okay? Now let's look at what Milan Lesic said.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can turn to 65 ter 32884.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And beginning at line 23. And again, Mrs. Mladic, I will read this out so that you can hear it in your language. "Q. Today we had a look at a video excerpt. The date was the 16th, and it was at the VMA in Belgrade. Do you remember what time it was when you went to visit Mladic on that occasion?" And Milan Lesic responds: "The time, sir, I'm not aware of the time. I remember that we came from Sofia first day in VMA, and I don't recall the time unless video or picture shows otherwise, and from the Belgrade when we -- the scanner arrived, scanner too, following morning we went to Pale. As well, I don't remember exact time. Was in the afternoon, as I believe, that we were there." So, Mrs. Mladic, both Milan Lesic and Ned Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- believe that this meeting at the VMA where you were present took place in the afternoon of the 16th of July and not as you provide now, which is late -- sorry, which is in the evening. So my question to you, Ms. Mladic, is this was a long time ago. This happened some 20 years ago. And it's really not surprising that you don't remember some details, but isn't it the case that you're also mistaken about when this meeting took place at the VMA?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not mistaken. I know when we returned from the wedding. And maybe they thought it was in the afternoon because it's summer time. The days are long. So they could not recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I intervene, as I did a second ago, it was in order to give Mr. Lukic an opportunity to object to the question. Mr. Lukic, do you still want to object or, the answer being given, can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was suggested that it's not surprising that Ms. Mladic does not remember, and I don't find it anywhere that she does not remember. And she just explained that she does remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you -- of course, you can suggest in a question something that is not in evidence yet, or even an alternative scenario. However, Ms. Hasan, this was 80 per cent of the question, rather -- and then only 20 per cent remained on the subject matter itself. That's not the balance we would appreciate most. You explained three, four, five times why Mrs. Mladic could have a different -- may have had a different recollection, and if you suggest that, no problem, but not three, four times and then ask the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you're claiming, Mrs. Mladic, that Milan Lesic and Ned Krajisnik are wrong?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's not possible that it was in the early afternoon hours. So if they think that after 6.00 is still the afternoon, because it's day-time, then that's it. But certainly ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Mrs. Mladic, I'd like to just -- I'd just like to understand. Now, when I asked you about the 14th of July about when your husband arrived, now what was it, in fact, that made you remember that he arrived to your home the evening of the 14th July and correct the earlier statement you had given to the Belgrade high court?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I thought about it a bit more. They called me in then. Perhaps it was a bit quick and maybe I couldn't really find my way. But when I gave this some thought, I came to that conclusion. I know that he left soon after that. He said, "I'm going to meetings," and it was still day-time for a long time after he left the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, in that answer you said: "I thought about it a bit more. They called me in then." Who are you referring to when you say "they"?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I mean when they called me in to -- I mean, Milenko Dundjar to give this statement. In July 2014.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So in July 2014 when you meet with Milenko Dundjar, it's at that point that you changed your mind about when it was that General Mladic arrived on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He questioned me for quite a while, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, in fact, it was during the process of questioning by Mr. Dundjar that it was suggested to you that, in fact, General Mladic hadn't arrived in Belgrade on the morning but rather on the evening of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Nothing was suggested to me. I came to that conclusion and that's the statement I made.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now were you aware, Mrs. Mladic, that it is the Defence's position in this case that General Mladic arrived on the evening of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes. He came in the evening of the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mrs. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the answer is not without ambiguity. The question was not whether he arrived on the 14th but whether you were aware that it -- that position that is taken by the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe Mrs. Mladic should remove her headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you understand the English language, Mrs. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's not the position of the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that Mr. Mladic arrived in the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could have objected to the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as phrased as such. Ms. Hasan, there is an objection against you putting to the witness what the Defence's position is, where this is now contradicted by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That he arrived to Belgrade, not to their home, and I will try to clarify it with Mrs. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's ... Ms. Hasan, apparently the -- no, one second. Mrs. Mladic. Apparently the issue is arrival in Belgrade and arrival at home on the 14th. That seems to be the -- what keeps the parties apart in view of what the Defence's position is. The witness has not answered the last question anyhow. If you would say, well, let's move on, as you suggested, but then it may be clear that your question has not been answered. At least --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not in an unambiguous way.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay, then I can --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, if you could answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have to ask Mrs. Mladic to put on the earphones again. Yes. You rephrase the question, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, you were aware, then, that it is the Defence's position that General Mladic was in Belgrade on the 14th of July in the evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was he not in Belgrade? Is that your position, Mr. Lukic? That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not only in the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it the Defence's position that he was there in the evening, notwithstanding that he may have been there earlier during that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then it's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then the objection was not justified, I would say. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan. Perhaps you repeat the question again and that you seek an answer. I'm now not inviting you to rephrase the question but to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, you were aware then that it is the Defence's position that General Mladic was in Belgrade on the 14th of July in the evening?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Well, regardless of that, now I am sure that he was in Belgrade on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "regardless of that," but the question is about that. Were you aware that the Defence, and apparently you agree with what may have been the Defence position then, that Mr. Mladic was in Belgrade on the evening of the 14th? Did you know that that was the position taken by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. It probably is. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And at what point did you understand that it was probably the Defence's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't thinking about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- "I don't know," "it probably is," so asking now when this witness was aware that it probably is, it cannot be connected in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you should have laid a foundation for that question which is not there at this point in time, because the answer of the witness could well be understood that she now, here, considers it a probability that it's the Defence's position. And then to say when, that, of course, we could have -- you could have expected the witness to say, well, just now. But I think she has answered the question. She didn't think about it any earlier, which I think everyone would agree hints at considering it a probability at this very moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Mrs. Mladic, were you aware that it is the Defence's position -- were you aware at any point that it was the Defence's position that General Mladic was not in Belgrade on the morning of the 14th as you had told the high court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you answer that question. Mr. Lukic, it reflects the position of the Defence? The first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then answer the question, Witness, whether you were aware at any point in time that it was -- it's the Defence's position that General Mladic was not in Belgrade on the morning of the 14th as you had told the high court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't talk about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you aware of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move on, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: During the meeting at the VMA, you recall, as you say in your statement, that Mr. Mladic was on the phone with someone. Do you recall who that was?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You provide, and this is at paragraph 7 of your statement, D1185, you say that: "I remember that while we were in the meeting at the VMA Ratko had a telephone conversation with someone. I recall that he did not order anything to anyone during the talks, nor did he use such a tone while he was talking on the phone." Now, you've seen the video that was taken during this meeting, which includes this telephone call; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Are you going to show the video?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you whether you have seen that video.

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I have seen it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did you see it recently? Did the Defence show it to you?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: They showed it to me when I was providing my statement in July 2014.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you recall that that video showed General Mladic on the phone; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. And I remember that he got up in that room where we were and he was using just a regular phone during the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did that video that you watched accurately reflect what General Mladic said?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to read you from the transcript of that video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is P01147. It's B/C/S page 90.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So that you can follow what I'm reading. Now, he gets on the phone and he says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shouldn't we also have the English on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I know you're going to read it, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it's page 94 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So he gets on the phone and he says: "Well, then, you should send Gojko. Have him come over tonight and send two more cars, two more cars and have them report here tonight. I'm not going while they're in the air. "Yes. "No, no, no, I know. "Okay, here's what we'll do. How about the stadium at Legenda's place? "Great, you don't have to send a car for me, I'll get there. Here: You send two cars, have them report tomorrow. They should leave in the morning, not tonight; two cars should leave at 8.00 and report to the VMA, to the Doctor Pero Janjic, Lieutenant Colonel; Milan Lesic and six others are to come there, yes." Now, I'll skip a bit. And he then asks: "Alright. How are the things up there, at Vinko's?" Now, Mrs. Mladic, that's Vinko Pandurevic he's talking about; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. Probably, but I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: But you know who that is? You know who Vinko Pandurevic is?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I don't know him personally, but I have heard of him. Yes, I have heard of him. He was an officer of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So then your husband goes on and he says: "Very well," I've skipped a line, "Very well, full steam ahead; maximum security and don't wait up for the orders; as soon as they show up in the air, shoot them down." And if we turn a page in the English, starting at line 1, he says: "Whatever, shoot them down at high altitude." Now, Mrs. Mladic, when General Mladic is on the phone and he is telling the person he's talking to "as soon as they show up in the air, shoot them down," that's an order, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I cannot say. I'm not versed in that, whether it's an order or not. Orders are usually issued on a secure line, and this is just a regular telephone. I think that he was talking, but he was probably talking about NATO planes that were in the air. And it wasn't safe. It wasn't safe for him to go now. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So the bottom is -- line is, Mrs. Mladic, that you really don't know whether what -- what qualifies as an order and what doesn't; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what qualifies as an order, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You go on in your statement and you say that you left the VMA, and this is at paragraph 6, but I'll read it to you: "We stayed in the meeting for more than an hour and a half. I remember that Ratko spoke with all the individuals at the meeting, which is why I believe that the meeting lasted longer than an hour and a half. We came home after the meeting and went to bed." Now, Mrs. Mladic, were you with your husband the entire time at the VMA?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was with him the entire time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you left together?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we returned home together.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You say, in your statement -- oh, sorry. Do you remember who drove you home?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Mladjo Kenjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you remember that night, you said, very well; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I remember that meeting, that there were about ten people there. I knew two of them: Milan Lesic and Dr. Pero Janjic. I knew the two of them personally. I didn't know the others. So I remembered meeting the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: But you remember going home with your husband that night?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And we were brought home by Mladjo Kenjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, were you with your husband the entire night?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were together the entire night. We went to sleep together and then we woke up together in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What time was it that you came home, that you arrived at your apartment after the VMA?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but it was approximately -- it was definitely after 9.00 or 9.30. It was after 9.00 in the evening, approximately. I cannot give you an exact time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What time did you go to bed?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Soon after. We were tired. It was a long day. We were on our feet the whole day, from morning till night.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you didn't do anything between your arrival at your apartment and going to bed? You just got ready for bed?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, nothing special. We maybe had some refreshments, we got ready for bed. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You said that it was approximately -- it was after 9.00 or 9.30 in the evening that you arrived at your apartment. Now, you say that you did nothing special. You got some refreshments and you got ready for bed. Did your husband engage in any other business that night?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, not that evening. He didn't do any work. Mostly when he comes to Belgrade, he comes to attend meetings and then he spends time at home. He would be just coming for a short while, then he would go quickly for meetings, and coming back.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So when you were -- when you say he didn't do any work that evening, Mrs. Mladic, did your husband, I take it then, didn't take any calls that night in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't take any calls. Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did your husband make any calls that evening in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't call anyone from the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Mladic, when you were at the VMA you said you were with your husband the entire time. Once the meeting was completed, okay, in the boardroom that you were in, what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Nothing. We took the lift down and we went to the car and then we went home. We didn't do anything special.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recall having visited the wounded in the hospital either before or after that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember, really. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So after your -- you finish with the boardroom meeting, you take the lift, you go down, and you were with General Mladic the entire time. Did he make any other calls in your presence besides the call that he made from the VMA that we just discussed?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, there were no other calls.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, I have one document more to show you and then we'll be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, you're aware that there are the Banjica barracks near to the VMA?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear you. There are what?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Military barracks near the VMA, the Banjica. Banjica.

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Uh-huh, Banjica. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you are aware that there is a landing place for helicopters just near the VMA?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I -- I didn't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: But you were aware that your husband, in travelling to Belgrade at times arrived by helicopter; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I don't know how he got there. When he arrived, he just entered the house. He rang the doorbell and he went in. I didn't see how he got there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you have no knowledge of whether or not he ever took the helicopter to Belgrade or from Belgrade back to the RS?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge, no, about that. I would see him off at the door, he would leave, I don't know who would drive him away or bring him home.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you tendering the last document?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I don't think she was able to comment on it, so I think we can save it for another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may just make one correction, which is the RFA that the OTP had sent for the war crimes department to conduct an investigation was to look into the filming and photography of the wedding ceremony and the reception, not, as I stated, the video of the VMA. We just checked that in the RFA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's hereby corrected. Mr. Lukic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. Not too many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Mladic, how many times in your life were you the matron of honour at somebody's wedding?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: This was the first time for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On working transcript page 49, line 9, something was suggested to you, and I'm going to ask you this: Do you know whether on the 14th of July, 1995 General Mladic came to your home in Belgrade directly from Bosnia, or did he previously attend some meetings and do you know that?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he came straight from Bosnia or from some meetings. He didn't have a lot of time. He didn't stay long. He said, "I'm going to a meeting with President Milosevic and some representatives of the international community." This is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether he was attending any meetings before that or not? Maybe you have no knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like us to take a look briefly at this document, P1147, transcript. The transcript that was before you. It contains this conversation, too, that was transcribed. Or rather, written down. This telephone conversation from the VMA. You were asked whether General Mladic gave any orders to this man over the telephone, and you said I don't know what an order is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 90 in B/C/S and page 94 in English. We have a problem with the translation, part of it. And now I'm going to indicate the part where we have a problem. And I'm saying -- well, it is where General Mladic starts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "Mladic ..." And then underneath it says: "Mladic, telephone conversation." In B/C/S it is line 4, underneath the second time the name "Mladic" is typed out. Line 6 in the English version. In the English version, it says: "[In English] Okay. Here is what we'll do ..." [Interpretation] And now I'm going to read out the B/C/S version, what it was that General Mladic said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is there a translation issue? Because you are -- you are using -- if there is, it's not through a witness that we resolve translation issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness was questioned exactly on this portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you should refrain from any of those comments. You should read to the witness what, in your view, is the best version and ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the only version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to hint at any discrepancy or whatever. You just follow up on what was done. And there is no way that in re-examination you could suggest to a witness that there are translation issues. There may be. They can be resolved. But then you read what, in your view, is the right version, and then we check later on - you can check as well, and we don't need the witness for that - whether the translation is correct or not. You can do that on the spot if you have any problem, but first put to the witness what is the correct version in this document. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is recorded here is that General Mladic said: "Okay. You and I will agree ..." This is what I'm going ask you: Were you ever out in the field where General Mladic was during the war?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him in Bosnia when he was issuing orders?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When he issued orders, did he say to his subordinates that they will agree on something, or did he tell them what they would do?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, he would tell them what they should do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just for me to be able to follow. Can you refer us into the English where --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- you say "can we agree"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no such a thing in English. That's exactly the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English it says: "Okay. Here's what we will do." It's the sixth line under second name -- line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S it says, I will quote [Interpretation]: "Okay. You and I will agree ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to thank Mrs. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it that you would like to have reviewed the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of this portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas you suspect that where it says "here's what we will do," is that some kind of an agreement should be part of the translation. Okay. That's -- I think it's a P exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, Ms. Hasan, you are aware now of the potential problem in translation, and I take it that you will have it reviewed and report to the Chamber. Then, Mrs. Mladic -- yes, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just put one question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you have another question. The Chamber has no questions. Further Cross-examination by Ms. Hasan:

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Mladic, the portion where it says, which Mr. Lukic just brought up to you, following that, your husband talks about "how about at the stadium at Legenda's place?" Now, do you know Legenda?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware that Legenda's place is in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had mentioned that General Mladic would not have flown that night for fear of being shot at. Now, you understand that flying to Zvornik would not have posed a threat to General Mladic as he would not be flying near the area of Zepa, where the NATO aircrafts were?

utterances.speaker: BOSILJKA MLADIC
utterances.text: But he stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I've nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. Ms. Mladic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. Mr. Lukic, is the Defence ready to call its next witness after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are. And my colleague, Ivetic, would lead our next expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the Defence will call now Mr. Dosenovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait for him to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dosenovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I take it. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you. May I invite you, and take your time to put on your glasses, to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dosenovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You'll find him standing to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to first please state your full name, first and last, for purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Mile Dosenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would next like to look at 65 ter number 1D5848 with you. While we wait for it, it should be a copy of your CV.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, have you had occasion to review the document that is now on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the information I provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you believe everything to be correct and up to date in terms of this information?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask just a few questions about your education, first. It's listed here that you attended the communications school for junior officers in Ljubljana. What kind of communications were the subject of your studies at this school?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I completed the communications school for non-commissioned officers in Sentvid in Ljubljana. It was a school for NCOs, communications NCOs in the JNA. We would have two or three specialties, radio telegraphy, telephones, and sometimes radio relay. We get this basic knowledge concerning communications. And from there, people became squad leaders in the JNA in communications units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we look at the entry for the military academy of ground forces communications department in Belgrade, it is listed that you spent four years there. How many of those four years were devoted to communications?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I spent four years at the military academy of ground forces, and the curriculum is the same for the first three years. And then communications were studied within that framework, but that would be for all services. And then it was only during the fourth year that one specialised, depending on the service involved, and I attended training for communications officers for one year in Belgrade. And that is where we were trained for the overall system of communications. So there was no sub-specialisation, as it was, in the school for NCOs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you to focus your answers very much on the question, because the simple answer to the last question would have been one year out of the four. The question was how many years were devoted to communications.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, four years of schooling at the military academy; three years of general training, all the same for all the services. General military training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you to further elaborate on your answer. I'm trying to keep you focused on what is asked, that was just how many years were dedicated to communications. And you went far beyond that. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page in English, and it starts at the bottom of this page in B/C/S and goes to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see here you were a teacher of tactics at the Communications School Centre in Belgrade. First of all, under what organ did that school fall under?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: The School Centre for Communications was within the JNA for training personnel for the communications service. I assumed my duty as teacher of tactics within the tactics department at that school centre. Within that department, there were several different streams; teachers for high schools, teachers for higher schools, and teachers for post-secondary schools. I was in the group of teachers for post-secondary schools. And if necessary, I also taught down there for secondary military schools and higher military schools because I was qualified to teach at all levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in terms of the tactics, what kind of tactics are we talking about here that you taught?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Tactics in communications means training personnel how to use personnel and equipment from a tactical point of view. That is the very basis of this training, how equipment should be used and how personnel should be used in certain situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if you could just clarify for us. You said that you were in the group of teachers for post-secondary schools. Who most often were your pupils? At what level were they?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Post-secondary schools? Well, most reserve officers of the JNA. That's that, this post-secondary education. Sometimes there would be groups for courses, different courses. And then sometimes there was NCOs, lower-ranking officers, and then I would teach that subject too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the second page in the Serbian. And the next entry that we see is at the same school as officer in charge of studies and improvement of curricula. What duties in relation to communications did that position entail?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I was assigned from the tactics department to the teaching and scientific development, and I was supposed to be in charge of studies and improvement of curricula. The basic aim was to develop curricula, then to see how the subject matter was being dealt with, acquired, also if it is necessary to make certain improvements. And also the library falls under this department for scientific development. And I would always be the first to look at the literature that came in, and I was trying to find the best ways and means of improving the teaching there. This was basically my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I see also that at some point in time for part of 1992 and 1993 you were a teacher of tactics at the Yugoslav Army School Centre. What subjects did you teach at that institution at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the so-called hot beds of crisis in 1991 for Slovenia, then Kupres, within a unit, that was called the 11th Operations Group. And then from there, in 1993 -- no, 1992, went to Drvar. However, because of certain family problems, I had to go back to Belgrade for a while. Again, I worked at the tactics department until I returned yet again to the 2nd Krajina Corps. I taught at the department as I've already explained -- as I already explained the first time, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at the time-period that you were chief of communications of the 2nd Krajina Corps, what was your rank?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I became chief of communications of the 2nd Krajina Corps in October 1993, as lieutenant-colonel. In June 1994, I got the rank of colonel and I remained with that rank and in that position until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would tender 1D5848 as the next Defence exhibit at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5848 receives number D1186, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1186 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to ask you: Were you tasked with drafting an expert report for purposes of the Mladic case?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I was given a task at the request of the Defence of General Mladic to write this paper that you have now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up in e-court 1D05787. And I do have another copy in hard copy for the witness, if he needs it. I'm told, I think, that the witness already has his copy in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, is that accurate? Do you have your copy in court?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then now we also have it on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that a clean copy, Witness, or is there anything written on it by yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are notes that I wrote myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then would you please put them away, and you will receive a clean copy which you may consult if you need. Because the parties and the Chamber should be aware of what is in front of you when you answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a few more, just, documents, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you put away all other documents and just ... If you want to consult any of the other documents, you should address the Chamber and ask for permission to do so and explain why you need to do it. Not to say that you're not allowed to do it, but we would like to know what you're reading before you answer questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with the document that we now have in front of us and of which you've been given a clean hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with the document. I drafted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, during proofing in preparation for today, did you have occasion to review the report with me to check for any corrections that were needed to the same?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I did look over it. There are some corrections that need to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can first turn to page 32 in the English, page 47 in the Serbian, and focus our attention, once we get there, on paragraph 10.16.5. And, sir, focusing your attention to the last full sentence in this paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could not broadcast the same, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what correction you had to this section.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: The sentence should read: "When the strength of the VHF radio wave weakens, such a wave does not shift to a lower frequency and such radio waves cannot fully bend to follow the surface of the earth."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we have the document on the screen without broadcasting it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it right that we are moving from page 32 to 33 for the relevant portion?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. It starts on page 32 and then goes to 33. I was looking at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We start at the very last line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, in relation to this paragraph, staying with this paragraph, are there any other corrections that you wish to make us aware of?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Footnote 41 on this same page. The number of the document has been mixed up. 47. I need to see which page that is. Page 53 in my version. Those two documents were switched and that's evident from the actual text.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And going back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that footnote 41 still?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Footnote 41 and footnote 47 I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What has been switched?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The contents of the footnote, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we should read the content of footnote 41 as it appears in footnote 47 and the other way around?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to paragraph 10.16.5, are there any other clarifications or corrections in relation to the same? And that's back on page 47 of the Serbian original.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to paragraph 10.16.5, is there any other clarification or correction that you want to advise us of as to that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as the paragraphs are concerned, I don't have any more changes that I would like to make or corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about as to the placement of this paragraph, 10.16.5?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I had that in my own document. This whole paragraph, when the work was being done, has been transferred to chapter 11. So I would like to place this paragraph as the first one in paragraph 11 and to be deleted from this section that is marked with paragraphs 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 56 in the Serbian and page 37 in the English, and focus on footnote number 48, I would ask you what corrections you have as to that particular footnote; footnote 48 of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: When the work was being done on the study, something has been dropped out, and these are the radio relay directions of the Drina Corps. I mentioned all of them and said how many channels they had, but I think page 2 there has been omitted. So what I would like is to have that page put back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me see if I can clarify with you. Are you referring to the recitation of channels that appears in paragraph 11.12.1 of your report? That is in the B/C/S at the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If the document were to be shown, you would see that that is the second page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now looking at the actual footnote itself, there are three documents or ERN numbers that are given as the source for the information in this paragraph. Do you have a correction as to the documents that are listed, these three documents in footnote 48 of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I just need an addition, actually. No changes. These are documents that the last digits are 91 and 92. This second page has been omitted.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another correction. This third document referred to in this footnote, there has been a permutation of the numbers in the last one, 0426 and 0734, but it should read 07 -- 7034.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could try to resolve the matter where the interpreter said the witness be asked to repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in relation to the two pages where you said the second page had not been recited in your report, the interpreters asked you to repeat the numbers. Could you please do so to allow the interpreters to get the accurate information.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: It's document number 0431-4791. And the second page of that document, 0431-4792. That page has been omitted. So I'm just asking that to be added to this paragraph 11.12.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To assist those of us using the numbers from this case, that document at issue that is being discussed is D00879 in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a bit puzzled by where the witness says that that page has been omitted, whereas in the footnote I find a clear reference to that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may have a clue to what --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how to resolve it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do that, then that would be your last job for today, at least in this courtroom, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you say that the second page has been omitted, are you talking about in the footnote or somewhere else in your report?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: I have that document in front of me, number -- this first number. That's the first page. Page 2 is under a different number. It's been cited but it hasn't been put into this paragraph 11.12.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So when you say that the -- a document has not been put into the paragraph, are you commenting upon the listing of radio relay routes and channels that is in paragraph 11.12.1 which cites to footnote 48?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, that's still pretty unclear to us, because what we see is a six-line description of radio relay routes and then a footnote with three sources. That's footnote 48, which is attached to the last one. But where then that document that -- that page which appears in the footnote, how is that to be linked to what part of this listing is entirely unclear. Perhaps -- I saw that there was a kind of a proofing note matter. We'll check whether it becomes clear from now. If not, then you should try to assist us in a better way tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we'll adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we'll adjourn for the day and we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning. I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever it may be about your testimony. You should not speak or communicate, whether that's testimony you've given today - very limited - or that's testimony still to be given tomorrow. If that is clear to you, you're invited to -- if that's clear to you, you may follow the usher. And if you want to take any of your papers that were -- more or less you were deprived of by the usher, then, of course, you are free to take them with you. See you tomorrow morning, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.
